question: Should Discord Activity support continue from this stale branch, move to the newer broader Discord Activities PR, or restart as a Canvas-plugin-owned design with a fail-closed Activity auth model?
rationale: The remaining blockers cross plugin ownership, Gateway auth, token handling, and operator config shape; automation can identify the defects but should not choose the permanent security/product boundary.

options.title: Rebuild under Canvas plugin auth
options.body: Port the work to `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require an explicit Activity credential path, avoid URL tokens, and add bounded fanout plus live Discord proof before merge.

options.title: Continue through the newer PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/65205 as the working branch only after resolving its similar security, compatibility, and merge-conflict blockers.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Leave Discord Activities out of core until maintainers settle the security model and whether this belongs in the Canvas plugin or an external package.

recommendation.title: Rebuild under Canvas plugin auth
recommendation.body: Port the work to `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require an explicit Activity credential path, avoid URL tokens, and add bounded fanout plus live Discord proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The key unresolved choice is the Canvas plugin/Gateway auth boundary that recent Canvas migration history points to `steipete` owning most strongly.
